candidates.summary: publishedKinds bounds the walk with ExtensionKindsUpTo(limit) before dropping view-less kinds, so a view-less hook inside the window silently shrinks the event and badge sets and defeats both caps
candidates.failure_scenario: Issuer registers one view-less hook, then maxEventKinds+1 (17) viewed kinds. Register calls publishedKinds(token, 17), which walks 17 kinds and keeps 16, so the 'too many extensions' abort an all-viewed 17-set hits never fires and the register event lists 16 of the 17 kinds GetExtensionKinds reports, with nothing marking it partial. Same on the page: 1 view-less + 10 viewed renders 8 badges and no elision mark although 10 are published, since i == maxBadges is never reached.

candidates.summary: ExtensionView is a linear lookupExtension scan and publishedKinds pairs it with every kind, so GetExtensionKinds costs n^2/2 over an issuer-chosen count and passes maxGasQuery near 2100 hooks
candidates.failure_scenario: An issuer of a registered collection adds view-less hooks across several transactions (each RegisterExtension costs O(n) for its duplicate scan). grc721reg.GetExtensionKinds(key) runs publishedKinds(v, 0): ExtensionKindsUpTo(0) returns all n kinds and ExtensionView(kind) re-walks the slice to index i for each, n(n+1)/2 iterations. Measured: 200 hooks cost 28.1M gas, 400 cost 107.3M (x3.81 for 2x n); extrapolated, about 2100 hooks put one call over maxGasQuery 3_000_000_000, so a query or a realm call reading that key's kinds aborts, a consumer looping over the registry included.

candidates.summary: RegisterExtension accepts a view that is itself the hook, and ExtensionView now hands it to any holder of the published *Token, where a type assertion to grc721.Extension exposes OnMint/OnTransfer/OnBurn
candidates.failure_scenario: A third-party extension written as one type implementing both interfaces, the shape grc721reg's own stubView models with RegisterExtension(view, view) at grc721reg_test.gno:277, 355 and 502, is registered. Any realm calls grc721reg.GetExtension(key, kind), asserts the view to grc721.Extension and calls OnTransfer(victim, attacker, tid); the hook takes no rlm, and per the borrow rule its writes land in the issuer realm's storage, so an index or royalty book the hook keeps is forged. The shipped royalty, metadata and enumerable split hook and view into separate types and are not affected; latent for third-party extensions.
candidates.verify_by: Filetest: realm A registers a combined hook+view that counts OnTransfer calls and registers with grc721reg; realm B calls GetExtension, asserts grc721.Extension, calls OnTransfer; expect A's counter to move. Fix: in RegisterExtension, panic when view.(Extension) asserts ok
candidates.evidence: grc721reg_test.gno:25-31 stubView implements ExtensionKind, TokenID, OnMint, OnTransfer, OnBurn; registered as ledger.RegisterExtension(view, view) at lines 277, 355, 502. Shipped views (*Royalty, *Metadata, *Enumerable) expose only read methods per grep of their func receivers.

candidates.summary: RegisterExtension freezes but never validates the kind, while NewToken validates name and symbol; kinds are now published on *Token through ExtensionKinds and each consumer re-defends
candidates.failure_scenario: An issuer registers a kind that is empty, carries control characters or backticks, or runs to kilobytes. Token.ExtensionKinds and grc721reg.GetExtensionKinds return it raw; grc721reg guards length only in Register, so a kind attached after registration skips that check and reaches every consumer of GetExtensionKinds, which must re-escape and truncate on its own as grc721reg's Render does with md.InlineCode and maxKindLen.
